messages.subject: Shiny Server API including file transfer?
parts:
Dear all,

thanks a lot for Shiny, it's an amazing framework, I love it :)

I have 2 questions regarding the interaction with the server as I would love to interact with it via a small web application I've built:

(1) Is there a RESTful or other API that can be used to interact with the server, i.e. to create a new app, push my R code or data files to this app? If not, will it come later this year?
(2) If not, how would you currently automate creating a new app, or pushing files to this app?

I very much look forward to your replies! Thanks so much in advance,

Ignacio

University of Cambridge

messages.author: c6ca7877bef91eef
messages.subject: Re: Shiny Server API including file transfer?
parts:
I create my apps locally and then push it to github and glimmer (the shiny server hosted by rstudio). To do this, I have a makefile in my app directory, which looks something like this. Typing make deploy pushes the contents of the repo to github, as well as rsyncs it with glimmer.

username: ramnathv
repo        : testshiny

deploy:
   git push g...@github.com:$(username)/$(repo)
   rsync -avz --delete . ramn...@glimmer.rstudio.com:~/ShinyApps/

Hi Ramnath,

thanks a lot for getting back to me. I agree that that's one way of doing it. However, what I would like to do is to have a web interface to building my shiny app. Ideally, I would like to have:

* a web-based editor for server.R and ui.R - only for these files, not for others (similar to Yihui's notebook example) that saves changes automatically to these 2 files in the respective shiny app folder
* some facility to push the files I've uploaded to my server from this server to the respective shiny app folder. I know that R can read files from HTTP URLs but, ideally, I would like it to be a secure connection so I don't have confidential data lying around publicly on the web

Any ideas?

Thanks so much again for your help! Best,

Ignacio

You could use RStudio server on glimmer and create a project for your app: http://glimmer.rstudio.com:8787/

* some facility to push the files I've uploaded to my server from this server to the respective shiny app folder. I know that R can read files from HTTP URLs but, ideally, I would like it to be a secure connection so I don't have confidential data lying around publicly on the web

As Ramnath suggested, you could use rsync (over ssh). If you're editing files directly on Glimmer, this step won't be necessary (but it's probably a good idea to have a copy on your local machine anyway).
 
-Winston

messages.author: c6ca7877bef91eef
messages.subject: Re: Shiny Server API including file transfer?
parts:
Here is one way to get this workflow functional.

1. Create a Dropbox folder (say myshinyapp)
2. Add ui.R, server.R and other files for your app.
3. Share dropbox folder with your collaborators.
4. Add a makefile to your repo

   username: ignacio
   appname: myshinyapp
  deploy-glimmer:
   rsync -avz --delete . $(username)@glimmer.rstudio.com:~/ShinyApps/

5. If you want git and github as well
   (a) Initialize Repo, Add Files and Commit

       $ git init && git add . && git commit -am 'initial commit'

 (b) Add these lines to your makefile

    deploy-github:
      git push g...@github.com:$(username)/$(appname)


This will ensure that even if your coauthor's mess up, your work is backed up on Dropbox which saves versions. Moreover, everyone gets to work from their Desktop ensuring offline access. I don't see the need to run Dropbox from a server, but if there are specific advantages, I would certainly like to know.

Cheers,
Ramnath

Ramnath, I was thinking that if you add Dropbox and trust its previous version functionality, you can get rsync and git/GitHub out of the picture entirely. Everyone would just write directly to the app directory on their own machines (which would be in the shared Dropbox folder) and Dropbox would deploy it out to each collaborator's machine and to the server.

I imagine you would need to be pretty careful not to be working on the same file at the same time, though. I highly doubt Dropbox will give you as robust merging options as git in that case!

messages.subject: Re: Shiny Server API including file transfer?
parts:
Dear Joe and Ramnath,

thanks again for your replies. My apologies for getting into this again but I have 2 further questions. I understand that Ramnath's suggestion still requires me to do the development locally and run at least one command (i.e. the "make" command to run the makefile) manually from the command line. If we assume that I do not want to do that at all, but rather, I would like the workflow to be as follows, would this be possible?

(1) Collaborators use a custom web interface (with less functionality than RStudio but similar to Yihui's notebook where only one file is edited at a time) to edit the server.R and ui.R files (e.g. when they click save, the content of the text boxes is saved in the files)
(2) The two files server.R and ui.R are pushed to my GitHub repository via the GitHub API
(3) Using a Service Hook on my repo, the ShinyApp server is notified of a new push to my repo
(4) The ShinyApp server reacts by pulling the updated files into my respective shiny app directory
(5) The updated ShinyApp is ready

Is there any way of making this workflow happen? Moreover, re (1), is there a web-based open source R editor out there that is similar to Yihui's notebook and has less functionality than RStudio, i.e. allows to modify exactly one file at a time?

Thanks so much again! Best,

Ignacio

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Shiny Server API including file transfer?
parts: The custom web interface sounds like going through a lot of effort to have a worse editing experience, not to mention being completely unable to deal with merge conflicts (i.e. what happens if two people are editing at the same time?). By moving away from RStudio or something like it, you're also losing tab completion, help, source code execution, R prompt, etc. Are you certain your collaborators need that much protection? Wouldn't it be easier to just explain to them that they shouldn't edit any files but ui.R and server.R?
